slides.title: Data Access and Authority over Prices
slides.caption: Data capability is described in company statements. Pricing authority is disputed.
slides.description: Sales records flow from two restaurants toward shared infrastructure. Dashed return paths show alleged pricing authority. Customers compare the resulting offers and other alternatives.
slides.notes: The diagram is conceptual. The solid data paths summarize announced capability, not a verified account of every franchise deployment. The dashed paths identify the coordination question raised by the complaint. Establish who supplies data, who receives recommendations, who can change prices, and what happens when an operator rejects a recommendation.
slides.source: Initial complaint, filed November 23, 2026; company statements and source review. ../01_Resources/37_Pricing_Systems_and_Competition/SOURCE_REVIEW.md

slides.title: Evidence for a Pricing Claim
bullets: Identify separate owners, contracts, data permissions, and pricing authority.
Compare recommendations, actual prices, overrides, costs, and promotions.
Explain the counterfactual supporting any claimed customer overcharge.
slides.notes: Similar prices or a common vendor leave the mechanism unresolved. Adoption may respond to demand or costs, and nearby firms may react to each other. The DOJ and FTC's March 2024 statement in a separate hotel-pricing case argues that nonbinding recommendations do not by themselves defeat an agreement claim. It is an agency argument, not a ruling on Wendy's. Equipment-availability records do not supply transaction prices or agreement evidence.
slides.source: Initial complaint, filed November 23, 2026; company statements and source review. ../01_Resources/37_Pricing_Systems_and_Competition/SOURCE_REVIEW.md

slides.title: Noumena and Practical Standing
slides.caption: A complete statistical account would still leave practical justification to be defended.
slides.description: Four upper boxes distinguish established findings, recognized empirical gaps, unanticipated issues, and acknowledged epistemic limits. Recognition connects an unexpected issue to further inquiry. A lower box separates practical justification about ends, authority, and obligations.
slides.notes: Negative and positive noumena have distinct roles within the limits of human theoretical cognition (Kant, 1781/1787, B306–B311). Hidden preferences, comprehension, and unrecorded costs remain empirical questions. Qualitative evidence also belongs to experience. The Groundwork (Kant, 1785, 4:428–429, 4:451–453) provides distinct practical arguments about respect and the intelligible standpoint. Do not infer a specific hidden preference, harm, or duty solely from a limit of empirical knowledge. An unknown unknown has not yet been recognized. An acknowledged limit requires an argument about what a specified inquiry cannot establish. The phrase known to be the never known has that scoped role. Normative questions remain open to reasoned judgment; statistical non-identification can change with a new observable law.

slides.title: A Measurable Objective Still Needs a Justification
bullets: Predicting acceptance leaves consent and authority to be examined.
Fitting heterogeneity leaves the person’s reasons to be considered.
An average outcome leaves particular obligations to be justified.
Defend which end the firm ought to pursue or abandon.
slides.notes: Examine the specific pricing and data-center arguments. Preserve their actual welfare results and safeguards. The criticism concerns a transition from empirical success to a complete account of welfare or permission. Kantian respect and Scanlonian reasonable rejection offer distinct practical arguments. Neither institutional affiliation nor ease of computation settles their validity. The analytical task begins with ends and authority, then uses evidence to evaluate consequences and alternatives.

slides.title: A Spectrum of Ontological Adequacy
slides.caption: Assess the scope of an interpretation and the objects its decision requires.
slides.description: Five positions run from measurement as reality, through behavioral representation, institutions and procedures, agency and reasons, to acknowledged limits and justified scope. Three lower boxes apply the questions to household costs, price targeting, and cancellation. Positions carry no numerical distance or author score.
slides.notes: A small model can answer a narrow question well. Ontological laziness occurs when ease of measurement substitutes for an argument about what matters. Place a particular inference on the spectrum and name the omitted object that changes the decision. More variables alone do not improve its adequacy. Keep empirical mechanisms, practical reasons, and Kantian limits distinct.

slides.title: Measure and Claim in the Electricity Case
slides.caption: Precision cannot repair a mismatch between the measure and the claim.
slides.notes: The paper explicitly measures realized revenue per MWh and explains its choice. Household bills require quantities, charges, periods, and a causal comparison; affordability adds household resources and needs. Operating entry can differ from the timing of committed costs. Developer identity requires validation before being treated as a business-model classification. Preserve the paper’s positive findings and qualifications. The criticism concerns an interpretation that exceeds these objects, without establishing a motive for the authors’ measurement choices. The complete bill arithmetic appears in M2 §2.28.1 and M6 §6.35.

slides.title: Philosophical Objections to Reduction
slides.caption: The conditions and limits of theoretical cognition require a separate argument.
slides.notes: The arguments concern the grounds of observational knowledge (Sellars, 1956), structures beyond event patterns (Bhaskar, 2007), intentionality (Husserl, 1970), and reasoning appropriate to normative domains (Scanlon, 2009). The conditions and limits of theoretical cognition supply a distinct argument (Kant, 1781/1787). These positions preserve different roles for empirical inquiry. M9 §9.43 gives the source passages and applications. Publication selection toward tractable questions is a hypothesis requiring evidence about the research process.

slides.title: Marketing Dialectics: Examine the Premise
bullets: State the claim, its evidence, and the premise connecting them.
Examine the demand for a complete explanation.
A marketing analogy must preserve the scope of the original argument.
slides.notes: Transcendental dialectic concerns metaphysical cognition (Kant, 1781/1787). These marketing cases adapt the practice of examining premises; an ordinary empirical dispute is not a cosmological antinomy. The third antinomy does not imply that accurate purchase prediction proves lost agency. Critical examination may support, restrict, or reject a claim; no forced synthesis is required.

slides.title: Definitions Can Predetermine a Claim
bullets: Does cancellation mean a request or a completed action?
Does predicted acceptance establish permission?
Does a service label match its actual conduct?
Trace the definition, evidence, and inference separately.
slides.notes: M9 §9.19 connects Kantian examination of an inference to the conditions supporting it, and Confucian rectification of names to the responsibilities conveyed by a service description. These are applications of the philosophical accounts in §§9.3 and 9.11. Consistency can coexist with false premises. A model score does not establish the legitimacy of the action it predicts.

slides.title: Authority and the Customer’s Requested Outcome
bullets: A customer asks to cancel.
The firm requires a retention survey before accepting the request.
The agent follows the firm’s rule.
Assess the customer’s authorization and the justification for the condition.
slides.notes: Technical permission, company authority, customer authorization, and ethical justification concern different relationships. A valid execution record establishes what happened under the rule. Kantian respect for persons asks whether the means respect the customer’s purposes and reasons. Confucian rectification of names connects the stated service role with its conduct. A higher renewal rate leaves the legitimacy of an imposed exit obstacle unresolved. M9 §9.20 develops the argument.

slides.title: Commercial Results and Customer Claims
slides.caption: Causal, measurement, and ethical questions have different premises.
slides.description: Separate paths connect a practice to commercial effects and customer outcomes. A judgment about the practice also requires an ethical principle.
slides.notes: A randomized intervention can establish incremental purchases without establishing informed choice or customer benefit. The humanity formulation (Kant, 1785) supplies a distinct ethical question about treatment of persons.

slides.title: Advertising Response and Customer Reasons
bullets: A joint test concerns whether any advertising coefficient differs from zero.
Loan take-up leaves comprehension and borrower outcomes unresolved.
Examine the information, reasons, and refusal available to customers.
slides.notes: The public P-Bench task describes a randomized consumer-credit advertising experiment and a joint null for 13 content coefficients. No empirical p-value is replicated in this course example. Rejecting a justified joint null would not identify every effective feature or a psychological mechanism. Kantian respect for persons asks how the firm treats customer judgment and refusal. Confucian role responsibilities concern the lender’s use of informational advantage and response to difficulty. Welfare claims require evidence beyond take-up.

slides.title: Self-Interest Creates a Burden of Justification
slides.caption: A reason for scrutiny is distinct from evidence of misconduct.
slides.description: A material stake leads to independent substantiation and then a decision that can change with evidence.
slides.notes: Institutional checks can be designed to work under private-interest pursuit without assuming universal dishonesty (Hume, 1741). Interested commercial-regulation proposals warrant scrutiny (Smith, 1776). Requiring firms to substantiate customer-benefit claims is a contemporary institutional recommendation. A duty-based conflict is distinguished from ordinary opposing interests in §9.45.

slides.title: Commercial Rewards and Analytical Judgment
slides.caption: Specify the responsibility that a competing interest threatens.
slides.description: Employer rewards and responsibilities both influence analytical judgment. A decision affects users, whose effective challenge can change its objective and interpretation.
slides.notes: Commercial incentives can shape which outcomes are collected before they affect any coefficient. Valsan’s account locates a conflict in an interest that threatens judgment owed under a duty. The platform example also raises broader questions about power and consumer control. Scrutiny and safeguards can be appropriate before misconduct has been established.

slides.title: Reward Learning and the Scope of Evidence
bullets: Posting studies and reward experiments inform behavior.
Behavioral records do not measure dopamine release.
Habit and self-control evidence concerns specified interventions.
Evaluate the feed, the user’s purpose, and unwanted continuation.
slides.notes: Posting behavior responds to experimentally varied social rewards (Lindström et al., 2021). Dopamine-neuron activity is examined in a separate neuroscience setting (Schultz et al., 1997). Temporary incentives and user-selected limits are evaluated with an economic model (Allcott et al., 2022). These sources provide different evidence. None alone identifies clinical addiction caused by an infinite-scroll feature. The ethical question concerns the actual design, its consequences, and the user’s authority to stop.

slides.title: Reasons for Honoring a Stopping Instruction
slides.caption: Defend the factual and normative premises, then compare objections.
slides.description: Evidence about an overridden instruction and a feasible alternative combines with a principle of revocable authority. Comparison of affected people’s objections leads to a conditional ought conclusion and revision.
slides.notes: State the principle permitting a firm to override a boundary for revenue and compare it with user-directed continuation. A time-limited user, an entertainment user, and a worker or creator occupy different positions. Scanlonian justification examines reasons for rejecting principles. It is not a vote or a weighted sum of engagement. A Kantian assessment examines the maxim and the person’s capacity to set ends.

slides.title: A Synthetic Feed Decision
bullets: Fixed population: 1,000 adult user-days per design.
Endless feed: USD 0.314 contribution; 85.6% goal completion.
User controls: USD 0.236 contribution; 91.8% goal completion.
A stopping requirement changes the feasible set before ranking.
slides.notes: The constructed population contains 800 leisure and 200 time-limited users. Under endless use, leisure goal completion improves relative to the finite feed while the time-limited group’s completion falls. Disclosure alone is assigned identical outcomes for a logical comparison, not an empirical estimate. All counts use the original group denominators. A requirement to honor a valid stopping instruction needs philosophical justification outside the score.

slides.title: Justify the Practice Before Ranking Its Performance
slides.caption: A commercial ranking also needs a justified set of permissible actions.
slides.description: Proposals pass through restrictions concerning truthful claims, data use, and refusal before performance ranking. Customer evidence can require revision.
slides.notes: Kantian duties cannot automatically be replaced by a finite penalty in an objective function. The proposed restrictions are contemporary applications requiring explicit justification. Human review and measured outcomes provide evidence; they do not mechanically define autonomy. For pricing, state a maxim that identifies the purpose and means. Compare truthful use of a demand forecast with a hypothetical concealed pricing arrangement. Evaluate the customer's capacity to understand and refuse the offer. A profitable result supplies no premise about permission; these hypothetical maxims establish no finding about the defendants' intentions.

slides.title: Confucian Perspectives: Profit and Responsibility
bullets: Evaluate how profit is obtained and which relationships sustain it.
A trusted adviser or customer-care role carries standards of conduct.
Examine whether the claimed role matches incentives and practice.
slides.notes: The Analects (Confucius, 2015, 4.5, 4.16) places righteousness in the evaluation of gain; the opening of Mencius (Mencius, 2016, 1A.1) challenges an exclusive focus on advantage. The discussions in Analects 12.7 and 13.3 motivate trustworthiness and fit between names, roles, and conduct. These are contemporary applications of texts with historical political settings. A profitable exchange can serve both parties. In the restaurant case, compare claims of franchise pricing independence and customer benefit with actual authority and measured outcomes. Trustworthiness concerns the accuracy of that account. Examine how the pricing team handles evidence of customer losses and truthful employee objections.

slides.title: Truthful Challenge and Cultivated Judgment
bullets: Harmony can include reasoned disagreement.
Learning and reflection should discipline an AI-generated answer.
Good conduct depends on repeated practices as well as stated values.
slides.notes: The Analects (Confucius, 2015, 13.23, 14.22, 2.15) supports discussion of truthful challenge and reflective learning. Cultivable moral beginnings (Mencius, 2016) and deliberate effort, teaching, and ritual (Xunzi, 1999) provide different accounts of human nature. A modern firm can examine what its rewards teach employees to notice and whether an analyst can report an unwanted customer outcome.

slides.title: Synthetic Personas and Actual Consumers
bullets: Generated reactions can inform hypotheses about product needs.
Claims about customer preferences require evidence from the relevant people.
Customers need opportunities to express conditions and contest consequential interpretations.
slides.notes: M9 §9.18.4 examines whose judgments a firm claims to represent. Kantian respect concerns affected people’s purposes and judgment. Confucian trustworthiness requires a truthful account of what the evidence represents and responsible responses to objections. The M4 case holds overall rating distributions fixed while reversing the product ranking. Accuracy alone supplies no permission to substitute generated consent for a person’s decision. These are arguments about a practice, with no inference about the researchers’ motives.

slides.title: Agreement and Independent Reasons
bullets: Identify shared data, labels, and objectives behind agreement.
Check the claim against evidence with a justified reference.
Distinguish predicted behavior from customer purposes.
Justify the proposed action and the means used.
slides.notes: Several models can agree because they share conventions and information. In mHealth, agreement with a modal category measures reproduction of a recorded category system. It does not establish nutritional correctness. In retention, a prediction of payment does not establish customer consent or justify an obstacle to cancellation. Kantian evaluation examines the maxim and respect for choice; Confucian rectification of names asks whether a claimed service fits its conduct. These are course applications of the earlier philosophical discussions.

slides.title: Demand Information and Consumer Surplus
slides.caption: Synthetic market; expected dollars per market-day. Preferences and costs are fixed.
slides.notes: Holding the objective fixed while improving the demand signal can reduce consumer surplus even when firms retain independent pricing objectives. Holding information fixed and replacing those objectives with joint profit maximization makes a separate comparison about incentives. Total welfare sums the two monetary columns under the model’s quasi-linear preferences and excludes income effects, vendor fees, and externalities. Reproduce the solved values with evaluate_market.py and check the exact fractions before interpreting either comparison.

slides.title: A Choice Procedure Can Change Renewal
bullets: A direct offer and an offer preceded by questions can produce different choices.
The customer still makes the final selection.
An independent value measure determines whether an additional renewal benefits that customer.
slides.notes: Questions, defaults, or retention prompts can precede a fixed target decision. The welfare comparison depends on consumer values, stable response probabilities, and the procedure set. A renewal increase alone does not establish either benefit or harm.
slides.source: M8, Section 8.14, Marketing Analytics Lecture Notes. ../06_Lecture_Notes/modules/M08_Current_Topics_and_Integrated_Decisions.md

slides.title: Opposed Interests
slides.intro: Suppose renewal yields firm margin $\nu>0$ and costs the customer $\sigma>0$ relative to declining.
slides.interpretation: A higher renewal probability raises profit and lowers customer value under these stated stakes.
slides.notes: This conditional comparison holds the offer, monetary values, and relevant response population fixed. It does not infer customer harm from conversion alone. Additional time and authority costs require separate measurement.
slides.source: M8, Section 8.14, Marketing Analytics Lecture Notes. ../06_Lecture_Notes/modules/M08_Current_Topics_and_Integrated_Decisions.md

slides.title: Profit and Customer Value Can Move Oppositely
slides.caption: Synthetic probabilities and fixed stakes. Direct renewal is 20%.
slides.description: An optional procedure lowers renewal to 10%; another raises it to 60%. At firm margin 11 dollars and customer loss 10 dollars per unwanted renewal, the latter gains the firm 4.40 dollars and costs the customer 4 dollars relative to direct choice.
slides.notes: The direct-choice benchmark is distinct from the consumer-preferred procedure. Relative to the 10% procedure, the 60% procedure creates a 5-dollar customer loss. These probabilities and monetary values are imposed inputs, not observed customer responses.
slides.source: M8, Section 8.14, Marketing Analytics Lecture Notes. ../06_Lecture_Notes/modules/M08_Current_Topics_and_Integrated_Decisions.md

slides.title: Experimentation Selects the Commercial Winner
bullets: A fixed set of procedures has stable renewal probabilities.
Independent randomized samples estimate each probability.
With opposed interests, accurately selecting the largest rate also selects the largest loss in that set.
slides.notes: The result requires common fixed stakes, a fixed catalog chosen before the experiment, stable responses from experiment to deployment, and complete independently sampled outcomes. It does not say that every experiment harms consumers.
slides.source: M8, Section 8.14, Marketing Analytics Lecture Notes. ../06_Lecture_Notes/modules/M08_Current_Topics_and_Integrated_Decisions.md

slides.title: Evidence for a Small Cancellation Burden
slides.caption: Hypothetical summary statistics and prespecified five-second bounds.
slides.description: An imprecise nonsignificant estimate fails equivalence. A precisely estimated small positive effect can satisfy equivalence despite differing from zero.
slides.notes: Two one-sided tests at 5% require the 90% t interval within both bounds. A six-second reduction fails two-sided equivalence but excludes excessive added time through its one-sided upper bound. Choose the hypothesis and justify the threshold before observing the result. Completed-task time leaves failures and abandonment as separate outcomes.

slides.title: Public Reassurance Exceeds the Reported Evidence
bullets: HBS coverage states that the four large firms have not raised consumer electricity costs.
The reported cloud-owner coefficient is positive and imprecise.
Categorical harmlessness requires evidence that excludes consequential harm.
slides.notes: The verified communication is HBS Working Knowledge, November 12, 2026, and company dissemination remains unverified. It also acknowledges future uncertainty. Table 4 permits positive price effects and reports p=0.101 for the direct developer contrast. Misleading reassurance could weaken safeguards or scrutiny; attributing actual policy changes or losses to the paper requires separate evidence. The paper has positive findings in other specifications, so calling the entire paper a null result is inaccurate.

slides.title: The Same Average Can Conceal Unequal Burdens
slides.caption: Synthetic monthly cost allocations; fixed use and population.
slides.description: Uniform and concentrated cost allocations yield the same aggregate price increase. Neither allocation reveals authority to assess or contest the rule.
slides.notes: Both scenarios add USD 2,000 to bills for 1,000 households using one MWh each. Distributional evidence distinguishes the allocations. Agency evidence concerns access to reasons, review, correction, and remedy. The average price coefficient does not measure those relations. The complete calculation is in M6 §6.33.

slides.title: Ontology, Evidence, and Justification
bullets: Ontology: distinguish utilities, households, ownership, contracts, and authority.
Evidence: identify which claims the estimates and bounds support.
Justification: explain why affected people may bear the remaining risk.
slides.notes: A narrow price study can be valid within its scope. The category error occurs when its aggregate becomes a complete account of household harm or agency. Four named owners versus other owners is not automatically cloud provision versus colocation. Functional assessment of concepts asks whether categories serve the decision (Thomasson, 2025). Compliance with a rule, endorsement of its reasons, and authorization remain distinct.

slides.title: Respect for Persons Requires Honest Uncertainty
bullets: An interested party owes reasons for imposing costs on others.
An insensitive test cannot certify safety through nonrejection.
Preserve opportunities to challenge evidence and obtain review.
slides.notes: Kantian universalization examines a rule that advertises safety whenever a test fails to reject, regardless of sensitivity. Such a practice rewards weak measurement and undermines evidentiary trust. The humanity formulation treats households as persons capable of judgment. Confucian trustworthiness requires descriptions that match conduct and a responsible response to inconvenient findings. Self-interest motivates substantiation; it does not establish guilt or deliberate deception.

slides.title: Validity Leaves the Premises Open to Challenge
bullets: Suppose every revenue gain justified adoption.
A proven revenue gain would then support adoption.
The first premise grants revenue priority over other reasons.
Defend that premise to the people bearing the burden.
slides.notes: The conditional deduction is valid, while soundness also requires true premises. Evidence for the revenue effect does not establish the normative premise. Logical consequence differs from norms governing reasoning (MacFarlane, 2004). Justification to affected people requires a separate account (Scanlon, 1998). Ordinary empirical evidence remains defeasible and should be evaluated according to the claim actually made.

slides.title: Preserve Meaning Through the Argument
bullets: A purchase is evidence of a transaction.
Consent requires an account of information and authority.
A unit price and a household bill measure different objects.
Feasible, permitted, and obligatory actions require different premises.
slides.notes: Terms must keep their meanings across premises and conclusion. Willingness to pay, benefit, and acceptable treatment are distinct claims. A formal option can remain difficult to exercise or unknown. Permission does not establish an obligation. Record operational definitions, populations, and time horizons before evaluating a result.

slides.title: A Counterexample Must Preserve the Premises
slides.caption: Assess the original recommendation and its criticism through the same five steps.
slides.description: The diagram moves from a defined claim to its premises, a proposed counterexample, assessment of a missing premise, and a revised conclusion. The revision returns to the claim.
slides.notes: Use the exact source passage. A construction can demonstrate that an inference fails without showing that the constructed mechanism occurs in the actual setting. The critic should defend the added empirical or normative premise and state what evidence or reasons would change the conclusion. The optional argument record keeps these tasks separate.

slides.title: Write the Missing Premise
bullets: Nonrejection becomes harmlessness only by adding an unsupported sensitivity claim.
An owner-list complement becomes a business model only with classification evidence.
An arithmetic residual becomes a causal account only with identification.
slides.notes: Reconstruct each claim from its exact source. Table 4 and HBS coverage supply the reassurance example; Section 4.1 defines the owner groups; page 3 attributes the residual growth to named causes. Grant correct calculations before challenging their interpretation. A counterexample must preserve the stated premises. A reporting inconsistency, an unsupported extension, and a contradiction are different findings.

slides.title: Historical Agreement Leaves Future Costs Open
slides.caption: A synthetic capacity threshold changes extrapolation while preserving historical responses.
slides.description: Two functions coincide for normalized load from zero to one. At load two, the linear function reaches four dollars/MWh and the threshold function reaches fourteen. The shaded area denotes the assumed historical support.
slides.notes: The construction gives both accounts exact agreement throughout the historical support, yet the linear and threshold accounts imply different future costs. Choosing between them therefore requires an extrapolation premise or additional evidence; the construction itself estimates no actual capacity threshold. The paper acknowledges future uncertainty, a qualification that belongs beside any assessment of stronger public claims. Reproduce the comparison with logical_counterexamples.py.

slides.title: What Ought the Firm Do?
bullets: Identical bills can coexist with different opportunities to challenge a decision.
State the factual premises and the principle governing affected people.
Defend a conclusion about what the actor ought to do.
slides.notes: Payment records conduct under available conditions. Endorsement, permission, and ethical justification need further evidence or reasons. Contractualism compares principles through the reasons people could have for rejecting them (Scanlon, 1998). A hypothetical jurisdiction with inaccessible decisions can differ from one with an effective challenge procedure even when bills coincide. State the circumstances, identify a feasible alternative, and answer the strongest objection.

slides.title: Flat Average Prices Can Accompany Higher Bills
bullets: Average bill equals average revenue per MWh times mean use.
Synthetic fixed population: USD 100/MWh with bills rising from USD 100 to USD 110.
Causal claims also require an explanation of why prices and use changed.
slides.notes: The example holds 1,000 customer accounts fixed and raises monthly sales from 1,000 to 1,100 MWh with unchanged average revenue per MWh. It attributes no change to data centers. The paper recognizes realized payments and regulatory allocation. Its outcome is economically meaningful, but it does not by itself identify household expenditure, affordability, or welfare. Fixed charges can already enter its revenue numerator. Full code appears in M6 §6.35; the matched customer-month identity is in M2 §2.28.1.

slides.title: Project Status Does Not Settle Responsibility
bullets: Investment can create obligations before a center operates.
Cancellation may leave costs, developer guarantees, and a recovery decision.
Assess who authorized the risk and who can challenge its allocation.
slides.notes: A utility with zero operating additions can still be exposed to project-related costs. The missing premise is absence of preparatory obligations and later recovery. The Bloomberg ComEd report motivates examining the pipeline; contracts and regulatory decisions determine incidence. Those sources do not identify affected donors in the paper. A defensible critique requests dated project histories, donor weights, collected guarantees, and cost-allocation records. The comparison and its direction remain conditional on those facts.

slides.title: From Premises to an Ought Conclusion
slides.caption: Facts and a defended principle jointly support a conditional recommendation.
slides.description: Factual and normative premises enter an application question, followed by an ought conclusion. The strongest objection can send the argument back to either premise.
slides.notes: The hypothetical customer has made a verified cancellation request, and a secure prompt exit is feasible. The proposed principle respects valid withdrawal while requiring justification of remaining burdens. Assess fraud, service continuity, and implementation cost. A factual premise needs evidence; a normative premise needs reasons. An objection can change either.
slides.source: M9 §§9.30–9.32; selected readings on reasons and stakeholder obligations. ../01_Resources/15_Marketing_Dialectics/07_Stakeholders_and_Reasons/README.md

slides.title: Compare Reasons for Rejecting Each Principle
slides.caption: Compare affected positions and feasible alternatives; answer the strongest objection.
slides.description: Two columns compare mandatory retention with prompt secure exit. Each considers customer reasons alongside security and service interests. A surviving objection leads to revision of the alternative.
slides.notes: Reasonable rejection is a judgment about reasons under principles of general regulation (Scanlon, 1998). It is not a vote or an automatic veto. In this hypothetical case, optional offers preserve persuasion without imposing it as a condition of exit. The comparison assumes necessary protections can be supplied at reasonable cost. A surviving objection requires revising the alternative or the conclusion.
slides.source: M9 §§9.30–9.32; selected readings on reasons and stakeholder obligations. ../01_Resources/15_Marketing_Dialectics/07_Stakeholders_and_Reasons/README.md

slides.title: Stakeholders Beyond the Firm
bullets: Identify people affected even when they are absent from the dataset.
Separate managerial attention from the justification of a duty.
State each person's interest, supported exposure, and reason for objection.
slides.notes: Descriptive, instrumental, and normative uses of stakeholder theory require different arguments (Donaldson and Preston, 1995). Managerial salience depends on power, legitimacy, and urgency (Mitchell et al., 1997). Fair cooperation can generate obligations (Phillips, 1997), while general duties still matter for involuntarily affected people. A resident’s moral standing does not depend on the cost they can impose on the firm. Identify the actual relationship and defend the proposed obligation.
slides.source: M9 §§9.30–9.32; selected readings on reasons and stakeholder obligations. ../01_Resources/15_Marketing_Dialectics/07_Stakeholders_and_Reasons/README.md

slides.title: Whose Voice Can Challenge a Prestigious Claim?
bullets: Hypothetical headline: “Harvard/Wharton study shows no harm.”
Compare its reach with residents' access to records and technical help.
Require evidence for reassurance and a substantive answer to material objections.
slides.notes: The headline is a discussion construction, not a verified quotation or institutional endorsement. The HBS Working Knowledge article is the documented public communication. A prejudice-based credibility deficit requires evidence beyond unequal credentials (Fricker, 2007). Institutions that gather and assess testimony also require scrutiny (Anderson, 2012). Distinguish nearby residents, utility customers, and people bearing costs. Local experience can identify an outcome; causal attribution requires a comparison. Institutional prestige supplies no missing premise. Verify actual use of a claim in a proceeding before alleging that it silenced objections.
slides.source: M9 §§9.30–9.32; selected readings on reasons and stakeholder obligations. ../01_Resources/15_Marketing_Dialectics/07_Stakeholders_and_Reasons/README.md

slides.title: Mechanism Evidence and Public Reassurance
bullets: Calls and filings document recovery plans and competing claims.
The electricity paper itself permits recovery and positive spillovers.
Assess the scope of reassurance separately from the historical coefficient.
slides.notes: New 2026 disclosures raise questions about future costs and allocations beyond the 2020–2025 historical window. They do not overturn that coefficient by themselves. PSEG's February 2025 residential-bill statement concerns wholesale capacity and procurement, which is a separate channel from construction cost recovery. M6 §6.36 develops the causal comparison.

slides.title: Whose Account of Affordability is Missing?
bullets: Investor calls give management and financial analysts a structured voice.
Household experience and authority require additional sources.
An institution ought to substantiate burdens and address material objections.
slides.notes: Distinguish a factual recovery plan from the normative claim that affected people deserve examinable reasons. Consider the objection that excessive delay may obstruct beneficial investment. Retain credible offsets and feasible protections when evaluating that objection. Public comments and consumer-counsel filings can extend the documentary record; interviews require an appropriate separate design. Hsieh and Shannon (2005), https://doi.org/10.1177/1049732305276687; O'Brien et al. (2014), https://doi.org/10.1097/ACM.0000000000000388; Gale et al. (2013), https://doi.org/10.1186/1471-2288-13-117; O'Connor and Joffe (2020), https://doi.org/10.1177/1609406919899220; Braun and Clarke (2021), https://doi.org/10.1080/14780887.2020.1769238.

slides.title: When Ought a Research Claim Be Published?
bullets: Identify the evidence worth preserving and the interpretation needing support.
Compare a corrected release, further review, and rejection of the proposed version.
For a public error, assess a visible correction that preserves traceability.
slides.notes: A paper need not be released in a form that attaches unsupported reassurance to useful estimates. Fallibility supplies reasons to preserve criticism and inquiry (Mill, 1859). Registered Reports illustrate reviewing design before learning the direction of results. Contractualism asks which release principle can be justified to affected people, readers, researchers, and decision makers (Scanlon, 1998). Neither favorable nor unfavorable implications for a firm establish research quality. The remedy should address a demonstrated defect.

slides.title: Favorable Framing and Justified Acceptance
bullets: Pricing language may emphasize discounts, flexibility, or convenience.
Research coverage may emphasize reassurance about consumer costs.
Trace the selected comparison and beneficiary to supporting evidence.
slides.notes: The verified Wendy's February 27, 2024 statement describes intended digital-board uses and rejects plans to raise prices at the busiest times. The HBS article interprets an empirical study. The comparison concerns framing and the reasons for acceptance; it establishes no common campaign or motive. Assess actual offers, outcomes, uncertainty, and omitted conditions. A persuasive message needs a further justification when it affects public choices.

slides.title: A Cancellation Evaluation
bullets: Include a direct-cancellation comparison.
Record whether optional retention content can be refused before exposure.
Measure completion, elapsed time, subsequent charges, and customer value.
slides.notes: An effective refusal path and an independent value measure reveal dimensions hidden by renewals. A direct-choice arm helps isolate the effect of the preceding interaction.
slides.source: M8, Section 8.14, Marketing Analytics Lecture Notes. ../06_Lecture_Notes/modules/M08_Current_Topics_and_Integrated_Decisions.md

slides.title: Same Renewal, Different Customer Intent
slides.caption: Synthetic populations: 1,000 customers each, one renewal month.
slides.description: A and B each have 900 billed customers. A contains 880 wanted and 20 unwanted renewals; B contains 600 wanted and 300 unwanted renewals. Both have 100 not billed.
slides.notes: Intent is stipulated before billing. All-customer unwanted shares are 2% and 30%; among billed customers they are approximately 2.22% and 33.33%. These populations do not estimate a treatment effect or monetary welfare. Run evaluate_retention.py; full source is in Section 9.5. Missing intent stays unknown.

slides.title: A Welfare Comparison
slides.intro: Synthetic stakes distinguish profit from customer value.
slides.code:
direct, selected = 0.20, 0.60
firm_margin, customer_loss = 11, 10
firm_gain = firm_margin * (selected-direct)
value_change = -customer_loss * (selected-direct)
assert round(firm_gain, 2) == 4.40
assert round(value_change, 2) == -4.00
slides.check: Higher combined surplus can coexist with a customer loss under these assumptions.
slides.notes: The combined change is 0.40 dollars per potential customer in this example. The welfare result is conditional on the imposed values. A choice probability does not independently reveal those values.
slides.source: M8, Section 8.14, Marketing Analytics Lecture Notes. ../06_Lecture_Notes/modules/M08_Current_Topics_and_Integrated_Decisions.md

slides.title: Coding Exercise: A Marketing Evaluation
bullets: Reproduce the two populations with identical billed renewal.
Keep unknown intent separate and compare the relevant denominators.
State the evidence and ethical premise needed to justify the practice.
slides.notes: Run ../03_Data_and_Code/Marketing_Dialectics/evaluate_retention.py. The full program and five tests accompany M9 §9.5. The synthetic comparison holds the eligible roster fixed and calculates the stated retention outcomes. Compare the conditional profit and customer-value consequences in M8.

slides.title: Federal Cancellation Policy: Current Status
bullets: July 2025: the Eighth Circuit vacated the 2024 FTC rule.
February 2026: the FTC restored the earlier prenotification rule.
March 2026: an advance notice sought input on possible amendments.
slides.notes: Checked November 5, 2026. The court identified a procedural deficiency. The March notice does not establish a replacement obligation; the October 14 information-collection notice concerns the restored rule. ROSCA separately requires disclosure, express informed consent, and simple cancellation mechanisms for covered online negative-option transactions.

slides.title: Cancellation Rules Differ by Jurisdiction
bullets: California strengthened its Automatic Renewal Law on July 1, 2025.
New York City's separate rule took effect October 1, 2026.
Identify covered transactions, enrollment media, and sector exceptions.
slides.notes: California guidance describes online cancellation without obstruction for online enrollment. NYC Section 5-110.2 requires simple cancellation as easy as enrollment and bars obstruction or unreasonable delay. Retention offers are subject to those restrictions; Section 5-110.3 contains sector exclusions. These sources were checked November 5, 2026. See M8 Section 8.19.

slides.title: Research Frequency and Policy Importance
bullets: Social influence leads the selected literature clusters.
Exit friction can affect many customers even with few papers in the sample.
Choose safeguards using mechanism, exposure, and customer consequences.
slides.notes: Journal counts give each paper equal weight and do not measure market exposure or loss. The 48-paper primary sample is access-selected and largely coded for inferred dual use. The full DOI census contains 824 eligible records with 721 full-text gaps. See M4 Section 4.17 and M8 Section 8.19.

slides.title: Pricing, Reviews, and Delivery
bullets: Price-display rules require attention to the covered industry.
Reviews presented as customer experiences require truthful provenance.
Housing-ad delivery can create discrimination concerns beyond targeting choices.
slides.notes: The FTC fee rule covers live-event tickets and short-term lodging. Its review rule distinguishes business creation and purchase of false reviews from mere hosting. The DOJ Meta settlement addresses housing advertising specifically. These sources do not establish an identical rule for every marketing application.

slides.title: Pricing Language and Regulatory Evidence
bullets: Shelf infrastructure, price rules, and consumer effects are separate objects.
The FTC's January 2025 report describes research on pricing intermediaries.
Specify the practice and applicable authority before making a legal claim.
slides.notes: The US FTC Section 6(b) staff research summaries report preliminary findings. This research publication has no rule effective date and supplies no legal finding against firms in the earnings-call sample. Use the source-linked cases from M5 to identify operational facts still needed.

slides.title: Personalized Pricing: Policy Status
bullets: FTC: August 2026 proposal; October 2026 information-gathering inquiry.
New York: disclosure law in effect; broader restrictions await enactment.
Price gouging requires its own covered circumstances and legal elements.
slides.notes: Checked November 6, 2026. The FTC proposal cites the personalized-pricing study (Dubé and Misra, 2021, 2023). October 28 Section 6(b) orders do not establish violations. New York GBL 349-a applies to covered personal, family, and household purchases, with exceptions. S8623B/A9349B has legislative passage without recorded gubernatorial enactment. GBL 396-r addresses essential goods and services during abnormal market disruptions.

slides.title: Environmental Claims: Two Different Decisions
bullets: 2023 Shell ads: the ASA upheld the overall-impression complaint.
2025 Shell ad: the ASA accepted the contextualized communication.
Evaluate the particular claim, material context, and applicable standard.
slides.notes: UK ASA, June 7, 2023: omitted context about the balance of business activities made the overall environmental impression misleading; a separate electricity claim was not upheld. April 9, 2025: the later ad included higher- and lower-carbon activities and investment context and was not found misleading. Its ruling explains the applicable pre-April-2025 code wording. These are specific regulatory outcomes, not firm-wide ethical verdicts. Sources: https://www.asa.org.uk/rulings/shell-uk-ltd-g22-1170842-shell-uk-ltd.html and https://www.asa.org.uk/rulings/shell-uk-ltd-g24-1248246-shell-uk-ltd.html

slides.title: A Product Fact and a Portfolio Impression
slides.caption: The scope of the conclusion determines the evidence required.
slides.description: The product, portfolio, and future transition require different supporting information: comparison, denominator, and time horizon.
slides.notes: A true statement about one product can be insufficient to support a broader impression. The ASA comparison supplies an institutional case; the diagram is an original conceptual analysis.

slides.title: Digital Service and Feasible Customer Choice
bullets: Offer assistance while preserving a usable alternative.
Measure completion, customer time, and firm cost on a fixed roster.
Treat geographic usage as context for investigation.
slides.notes: An optional assistance intervention can expand feasible choices. A mandatory app workflow may impose equipment, registration, and verification costs. A proposed evaluation should record the customer’s requested action and channel and preserve the ability to refuse optional profiling. Geographic Windows usage does not observe those outcomes.

slides.title: Evidence and Authority to Classify a Customer
bullets: Kantian critique examines the move from area activity to individual ability.
Respect for persons requires reasons for restrictions and usable correction.
Confucian role responsibilities support responsive, humane service.
slides.notes: A stable cluster does not authorize a firm to remove an individual’s options. Examine the additional premise linking measured activity to a permissible action. Humane intent must be connected to the customer’s stated task and preferred channel, with an opportunity to correct classifications. The same area score can motivate assistance or exclusion; the consequences and authority differ.

slides.title: Reliable Measurement and a Worthy Objective
slides.caption: Unbiasedness and precision support factual premises. The goal and treatment of people require reasons.
slides.description: Reliable evidence informs a revenue objective. Personal reasons inform an alternative principle. Compare objections to both, including burdens, access, authority, and feasible alternatives.
slides.notes: Statistical unbiasedness concerns an estimator across repetitions of a specified design; precision concerns its dispersion. Both can protect people against mistaken claims. Even perfect measurement of all monetary consequences leaves a normative premise to defend before recommending revenue maximization. Normative reasons and reasonable rejection ground the ethical application (Scanlon, 1998, 2009). Statistical estimation retains its distinct evidential role. The same requirement applies to every institution and research method. The finding of lower aggregate customer surplus remains part of the evidence (Dubé and Misra, 2021).

slides.title: Rational Acceptance and Reasonable Objection
bullets: Instrumental rationality: an effective choice for a selected aim.
Reasonableness: a principle justified through affected people’s reasons.
Weak alternatives can explain acceptance while sustaining a strong objection.
slides.notes: Suppose an urgently dependent customer accepts a surcharge that a seller predicts exactly. The seller and customer can each act effectively for their immediate aims while the rule faces an objection to avoidable exploitation. Examine the feasible lower offer, the seller’s costs and risks, and the reasons of other affected people. Instrumental rationality is one sense of rationality; broader rational thought can include morality. Reasonableness is neither majority preference nor an unconditional veto. State what fact or reason would change the conclusion.

slides.title: Pricing and Public Reassurance
bullets: Personalized prices: predicted acceptance and authority to impose a burden.
Dynamic pricing: discount claims, full price paths, and usable alternatives.
Data centers: average-price evidence, household exposure, and a voice in allocation.
slides.notes: The practices share a need to justify consequential treatment to affected people. Personalization uses customer information; dynamic pricing can change a common price over time. Wendy’s documented statement concerns its announced policy, with implementation requiring evidence. The data-center case retains the criticisms of inference and public interpretation. Even exact knowledge of a narrow historical effect would leave future cost recovery, household bills, failed projects, and participation unresolved. Nearby residents, utility customers, and eventual cost bearers are distinct populations. Compare a rule allowing favorable evidence to close debate with proportionate substantiation and answers to material objections. Similarities do not establish identical harms or motives.

slides.title: Same Tested Demand, Opposite Welfare Signs
slides.caption: Synthetic population: L 60%, H 40%. Surplus changes are −USD 1.682 and +USD 0.682.
slides.description: Two panels share a zero-to-one probability scale. Solid blue and dashed orange curves match tested endpoints but enclose different areas as prices change.
slides.notes: The baseline price is USD 10 for both groups. The candidate schedule charges L USD 5 and H USD 20. Revenue rises from USD 6.20 to USD 6.70 in both completions. Quasilinear unit demand makes surplus changes areas under demand. Monotonicity bounds the population change between −USD 1.70 and +USD 0.70. Both completions harm H; finite support leaves the aggregate sign unresolved. This construction does not establish bias in the empirical paper.

slides.title: A Majority Benefits While a Minority Loses
slides.caption: Synthetic uniform valuations: discount-only pricing remains profitable and avoids H’s price increase.
slides.description: Horizontal bars show +USD 0.319 expected surplus per L member under both schedules, −USD 8.042 per H member under segmentation, and zero H change under discount-only pricing.
slides.notes: The benchmark is the optimal uniform price USD 19/3. L represents 60% and H 40%; group labels do not identify wealth or vulnerability. A quarter of H loses a purchase, equal to 10% overall. The capped alternative earns USD 6.133 per eligible person versus USD 6.017 under uniform pricing. A conclusion about serious deprivation requires facts beyond these invented valuations.

slides.title: A Defensible Scanlonian Pricing Argument
bullets: Identify the person’s burden and the facts producing it.
Compare a viable less burdensome principle.
Defend the ought conclusion against the strongest objection.
slides.notes: If a seller exploits serious need despite a viable lower offer and no comparably serious countervailing burden, the lower offer is supported by a strong contractualist argument. Monetary amounts inform reasons; they are not a moral score. The firm’s legitimate interests include service viability and the people dependent on it. Majority benefits do not automatically resolve the losing person’s objection.

slides.title: Mobile Targeting: Reconstruct the Incentives
slides.caption: RMB expected revenue per messaged consumer. Published model outputs, not new estimates.
slides.notes: The complete 4-by-4 table yields behavioral targeting as the sole pure equilibrium. A’s best-response margin against a geobehavioral deviation is 0.001 RMB when B uses behavioral targeting. The paper reports a 40% posterior probability that this deviation improves A’s profit. The rounded calculation recovers incentives under the model; it supplies no consent measure or evidence of an unlawful agreement. Original Python uses the transcribed published table. Replication microdata were not downloaded.

slides.title: Kantian Authority Over Location History
bullets: Specify the maxim, including any concealment or dependence.
Check permission, understandable terms, and usable refusal.
A useful discount does not settle authority over secondary data use.
slides.notes: The paper documents targeting from current location and historical visits. The course does not establish that consent was absent. A hypothetical maxim relying on concealed material use faces a Formula of Humanity objection because it defeats informed authorization. An understandable opt-in offer with meaningful alternatives requires a different assessment. The INFORMS download terms allow replication but restrict other reuse and the venue for a corrective follow-up; M9 §9.37 evaluates the reasons for those restrictions.

slides.title: An Antitrust Case Needs a Specified Mechanism
bullets: Section 1: evidence of agreement beyond parallel pricing.
Section 2: monopoly power and exclusionary conduct.
Match the injury and counterfactual to the challenged conduct.
slides.notes: A paper’s method or a model’s softening of competition does not establish a violation. In a hypothetical shared-pricing case, contracts, confidential inputs, overrides, and discount restrictions help distinguish coordination from independent decisions. Twombly concerns plausible agreement; Trinko explains why monopoly pricing alone is insufficient. Robinson–Patman’s commodity-sales scope does not generally cover recruitment services or movie admissions.

slides.title: Revenue Growth Differs from an Overcharge
slides.caption: The lawful counterfactual is assumed. Eight excluded purchases require separate welfare evidence.
slides.notes: The example assumes 100 counterfactual purchases at USD 100 and 92 actual purchases at USD 120. Invoice differences are based on actual quantities; revenue changes also contain a quantity component. No empirical damages or violation is established. A profit-maximizing uniform monopoly price is not automatically a lawful competitive benchmark. Comcast requires the damages model in that class-certification setting to match the accepted liability theory; Brunswick requires antitrust injury.

slides.title: Antitrust Proof and Reasons Owed to People
slides.caption: A remedy needs attributable injury, a feasible alternative, and justified treatment of affected people.
slides.description: One branch identifies legal elements and evidence. A second compares burdens and reasons. Both inform a remedy that preserves independent forecasting while ending a proved restrictive arrangement.
slides.notes: Scanlonian reasoning can explain why independent alternatives matter and why sanctions require reliable attribution. The firms’ workers, owners, and customers also have reasons to reject unsupported accusations. Courts do not apply contractualism as the antitrust test. Moral standing includes people excluded from purchases and can extend beyond a legally actionable claim.

slides.title: Legal Permission Leaves an Ought Question
bullets: A lawful unilateral practice can still exploit serious need.
An ethical objection does not supply a missing legal element.
Compare safeguards, alternatives, and who bears a mistaken decision.
slides.notes: The hypothetical remedy separates useful independent forecasting from a proved restrictive arrangement. A necessity defense must identify benefits that genuinely require the challenged feature and the people who would lose them. If a less restrictive alternative supplies the same benefits, that defense fails on its own premise. The RealPage record supplies allegations and proposed terms; the separately entered Greystar judgment has different status.

slides.title: Name What Would Change the Conclusion
bullets: New randomized cells can distinguish response models.
Independent valuations can narrow welfare disagreement.
Matched household evidence can support a narrower reassurance claim.
A serious objection can change the proposed principle.
slides.notes: Scientific criticism remains open to correction. For electricity claims, informative uncertainty bounds, a credible comparison, household outcomes, and documented recovery protections could support reassurance within their scope. For pricing, evidence about feasible alternatives and legitimate operating needs can change the moral assessment. Reasonable rejection concerns reasons from affected positions, not a vote or commercial acceptance alone.

slides.title: Personalization and the Learner’s Authority
bullets: Keep the source argument and consequential assumptions accessible.
Allow a learner to change representations and challenge the conclusion.
Evaluate independent reasoning and supported disagreement.
slides.notes: A student can reasonably object to an explanation that hides the premise on which its recommendation depends. A defensible learning system makes that premise inspectable and permits a reasoned objection. Response history does not exhaust the person or determine what the person ought to learn. Missing empirical measurements also remain distinct from the noumenal limiting concept (Kant, 1781/1787).
slides.source: M9, Section 9.44, Marketing Analytics Lecture Notes. ../06_Lecture_Notes/modules/M09_Marketing_Dialectics.md

slides.title: Whose Burdens Survive the Sample Restriction?
slides.caption: The affected population retains its standing when records are incomplete.
slides.description: The solid path runs from a household decision through the relevant population and causal comparison to a justified claim. A dashed shortcut from recent operating records leaves premises unresolved.
slides.notes: The proposed Scanlonian objection concerns an unexamined burden and the evidence used to justify it. The critic must also consider developer payments, asset reuse, and disallowed cost recovery. Phantom projects provide a concrete design concern; actual donor contamination remains an empirical question.

slides.title: Thoughtful Design Gives Reasons for the Comparison
bullets: A precise selected-population result does not settle the full burden.
Identify the missing empirical premise and the household’s objection.
Reconstruct the design or narrow the public claim.
slides.notes: In the synthetic savings scenario, the operating-project effect is minus 2 dollars/MWh while the equal-weight mean over completed, canceled, and pending proposals is plus 3.33. Each describes its stated population. Using one to reassure the other is the unsupported step. Missing project data are investigable empirical unknowns and should not be equated with Kantian noumena.

slides.title: A Dataset Has an Origin and an Intended Use
bullets: Created artifacts have histories and dependencies.
Distinguish a dataset version, a copy, and the people it represents.
Institutional production leaves accuracy open to evidence.
slides.notes: The artifact analogy concerns creation, identity, preservation, and recognized use. It does not make household bills fictional. Billing incentives can improve accuracy while classification and access rules exclude questions that matter to residents. A valid institutional charge remains open to moral criticism. The artifact analogy draws on created dependencies and public norms of use (Thomasson, 1999, 2014).

slides.title: Truth, Evidence, and Permission
slides.caption: A correct record supports neither a causal attribution nor a policy on its own.
slides.description: Three columns separate a recorded charge, a causal claim, and a recommendation. Semantic and legal premises establish the record’s meaning and status; epistemic premises concern measurement and counterfactuals; moral premises concern people, authority, alternatives, and reasons.
slides.notes: Ask students to supply the missing premise at each arrow. Logical validity does not make a premise true. Evidential warrant does not settle permissible action. Modal normativism does not claim that conventions make modal truths true (Thomasson, n.d.). Inductive risk concerns the stakes of error (Douglas, 2000); it does not authorize inventing adverse evidence.

slides.title: Who Ought to Produce the Evidence?
bullets: Residents may bear a burden while institutions control the relevant records.
A reasonable principle provides proportionate scrutiny and privacy protection.
An unsupported broad reassurance should be narrowed.
slides.notes: Develop the contractualist premises (Scanlon, 1998): material burden, informational control, standing to contest, and feasible alternatives. Test a privacy objection and propose controlled linkage with aggregate public results. Undone science concerns institutional research priorities; deliberate suppression requires additional evidence. Political sensitivity can motivate disclosure as well as secrecy. The introduced S. 5640 is a reporting proposal, not an effective duty. Effective critical interaction requires venues, uptake, public standards, and tempered equality of intellectual authority (Longino, 2004).

slides.title: A Decision with Consumer Outcomes
bullets: State the decision, affected people, and evidence.
Defend what the actor ought to do, with a normative premise.
Answer the strongest objection and name a condition for revision.
slides.notes: A recommendation needs a justified principle connecting evidence to action. Compare the reasons of customers, workers, households, and others affected by the decision. Distinguish a feasible alternative from an imagined costless option. An effective argument can disagree with the instructor while supporting its premises and answering objections.

practice: Defend a recommendation using factual and normative premises, an affected person's strongest objection, and a feasible alternative. Extended numerical and philosophical cases are optional practice.
application: Evaluate customer outcomes, public claims, and institutional duties through Kantian, Confucian, and Scanlonian arguments. Compare stakeholder reasons and opportunities to contest evidence. Personalized pricing, demand completions, Dubé mobile targeting, and antitrust proof with Scanlonian reasons. Compare rational acceptance with reasonable rejection across pricing and infrastructure reassurance, holding factual estimates fixed.

title: Integrated Decisions and Final Presentations
objectives: Connect validated analysis to a concrete marketing decision.
Evaluate uncertainty, consumer consequences, and operational constraints.
Communicate a reproducible conclusion and a useful next test.

slides.title: An Integrated Marketing Decision
bullets: Choose a feasible action and a defined customer population.
Connect measurement, modeling, and evaluation to that action.
State the costs, customer outcomes, and uncertainty that affect the choice.
slides.notes: A marketing decision may draw on a descriptive assessment, a predictive model, a causal comparison, and a scenario. Connecting these components requires explaining how each contributes to the recommendation while retaining its population, assumptions, and scope of inference.

slides.title: The Evidence Behind the Recommendation
bullets: State the sample, observation unit, and outcome horizon.
Show the comparison that supports the main claim.
Explain which result changes the recommended action.
slides.notes: A result becomes decision-relevant when it changes a feasible choice under explicit costs or constraints. The audience should be able to assess the supporting comparison directly.

slides.title: A Calculation the Audience Can Check
bullets: Trace one figure to an aggregate table and source records.
Reproduce one prediction, coefficient interpretation, or policy value.
Retain complete code and data definitions with the result.
slides.notes: A hand-checkable calculation complements complete reproducible code. It provides independent evidence about the unit, denominator, and direction of the computation.

slides.title: A Result That Could Change the Decision
bullets: Identify the most consequential uncertain parameter.
Show the threshold at which the preferred action changes.
Consider a feasible test that could resolve that uncertainty.
slides.notes: Sensitivity should connect uncertainty to action. A wide parameter range is useful when it reveals whether the decision is stable or fragile.

slides.title: Customer Consequences
bullets: Report effects on access, time, value, and unwanted charges where relevant.
Distinguish voluntary continued use from difficulty leaving.
Explain how customers can refuse or correct the proposed interaction.
slides.notes: The relevant customer outcome depends on the product and action. A higher platform metric can conceal costs outside the optimized objective.

slides.title: Regulatory Scope
bullets: Identify the jurisdiction and covered conduct.
Separate the current rule from a proposal or allegation.
Match the evidence supporting a claim to what customers will understand.
slides.notes: The primary-source record should identify the effective date and consequential exclusions. A legal conclusion for one sector or jurisdiction should not be transferred mechanically to another.

slides.title: Presentation Discussion
bullets: Is the recommendation supported for the stated population?
What analytical or customer risk has the largest consequence?
Which part of the result can be reproduced independently?
slides.notes: Feedback should name an observable gap in the evidence or a specific counterexample. The strongest response supplies a corrected comparison or explains why the original remains valid.

slides.title: A Deployment Comparison
bullets: Retain a benchmark and a defined evaluation population.
Monitor outcomes and data coverage after the action changes behavior.
Set a response when quality or customer outcomes deteriorate.
slides.notes: A policy that changes exposure can also change future training data. Evaluation after deployment needs versioned inputs, outcomes, and policy rules.

slides.title: An Evidence-Based Recommendation
bullets: Name the action, expected consequence, and decision threshold.
Keep consequential uncertainty beside the estimate.
Identify the next concrete extension supported by the evidence.
slides.notes: A conditional recommendation can be decisive when its conditions are measurable. The final decision should remain traceable to the data, assumptions, and customer outcomes.

practice: Presentation blocks with evidence, reproducibility, and customer-outcome discussion.
application: Compare recommendations using decision thresholds and identify the next useful test.
